item.title: YouTube Gold: Duke vs. St. John’s In The 1992 Elite Eight
item.description: UNITED STATES - MARCH 24: College Basketball: NCAA playoffs, Duke Bobby Hurley (11) in action, playing defense vs St, John's David Cain (11), Pontiac, MI 3/24/1991 (Photo by Richard Mackson/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (SetNumber: X41177) I n the 1990-1991 season, Duke was coming off an awful beating at the hands of UNLV in the 1990 NCAA championship game. Things were different, though. Duke had added Grant Hill, who would become the missing piece to a truly great team. The Blue Devils rolled by #15 Louisiana-Monroe, 102-73, #7 Iowa, 85-70, #11 UConn, 81-67, before running into #4 St. John’s in the Elite Eight. St. John’s had just taken apart #1 seed Ohio State 91-74 in the Sweet Sixteen and appeared to be on a roll. However, Duke was on a roll of its own and forced five early turnovers before taking a 40-27 lead into halftime. Bobby Hurley finished with 20 points and 7 rebounds, as Duke coasted to a 17-point win. Christian Laettner had 19 points, while Hill finished with 12. St. John’s really did get picked apart. Guard Chucky Sproling described Duke’s defense as a “buzzsaw,” and no wonder: the Blue Devils forced 26 turnovers. Go to the DBR Boards to find Blue Healer Auctions || Drop us a line

item.title: Top 10 Italy players in Serie A Week 8: Bartesaghi stars, Calò on target again
item.description: Top 10 Italy players in Serie A Week 8: Bartesaghi stars, Calò on target again Frosinone midfielder Giacomo Calò was the highest-rated Italy player in Serie A in the eighth round of 2026-27 fixtures that concluded on Sunday evening after netting for the second week in succession: Here is a look at the top 10 best-performing Italians from this weekend. The eighth round of Serie A fixtures began on Friday evening with Torino’s 3-2 victory at home against Monza and concluded on Sunday evening with Milan’s 2-0 win away against Udinese. Read Football Italia Ad-Free and get access to Exclusive News and Content – Free Trial – Click Here UDINE, ITALY – OCTOBER 25: Christian Pulisic of Milan is surrounded by teammates after scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and AC Milan at Stadio Friuli on October 25, 2026 in Udine, Italy. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images) According to the latest set of player ratings, Frosinone’s Calò was the only Italian player to be given a rating of 7.5/10 or higher throughout the weekend’s fixtures. He netted his side’s third goal in an eventual 4-4 thriller away against Atalanta on Sunday afternoon, the second week in a row that he has been on target and the second week in a row where the newly-promoted side have managed to score four in one game. Several other Italians have been given ratings of 7/10, including Milan’s Bartesaghi, who impressed with his performance in an advanced position on the Rossoneri left flank during their 2-0 win over Udinese. Among the other players to be rated at 7/10 or this weekend are Atalanta’s Marco Carnesecchi, despite conceding four against Frosinone, Lazio’s Mattia Zaccagni and Bologna’s Federico Bernardeschi. ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Mattia Zaccagni of SS Lazio in action during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Parma Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on October 24, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Top 10 Italy players in Serie A Week 8 Giacomo Calò (Atalanta 4-4 Frosinone) – 7.5 Marco Carnesecchi (Atalanta 4-4 Frosinone) – 7 Mattia Zaccagni (Lazio 2-1 Parma) – 7 Nicolo Casale (Cagliari 0-2 Bologna) – 7 Federico Bernardeschi (Cagliari 0-2 Bologna) – 7 Davide Bartesaghi (Udinese 0-2 Milan) – 7 Raoul Bellanova (Atalanta 4-4 Frosinone) – 6.5 Wilfried Gnonto (Inter 2-1 Fiorentina) – 6.5 Nicolo Barella – (Inter 2-1 Fiorentina) – 6.5 Matteo Politano (Napoli 3-3 Roma) – 6.5

item.title: Manchester United could look to former Premier League coach as Carrick replacement
item.description: Manchester United could look to former Premier League coach as Carrick replacement Manchester United Manager Search Intensifies as Michael Carrick Future Nears Decision Manchester United are moving closer to a major decision on Michael Carrick after the damaging 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, with pressure building rapidly around Old Trafford and senior figures now expected to accelerate succession planning. According to Sky Sports, the club had already begun weighing up alternative options before Sunday’s result, a reflection of how alarming this start to the Premier League season has become. Photo: IMAGO The latest setback leaves United on an eight-match winless run and hovering just above the relegation zone, an unthinkable position for a club of this scale. Internally, the sense appears to be that events are reaching a conclusion. Sky Sports reports that key decision-makers had been considering the head coach situation even before Bournemouth exposed United again, and the expectation from insiders is now that Carrick could soon be removed. That process will be shaped by director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada, who are set to make a recommendation to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Those lines of authority matter, because any change at this stage of the season would need to be fast, coordinated and backed by clarity over what comes next. United cannot afford another drawn-out period of uncertainty. Michael Carrick Under Severe Pressure There was a growing feeling long before full-time on Sunday that Carrick’s position had become deeply precarious. United were second best throughout against Bournemouth, and the wider context made the performance more troubling. Bruno Fernandes, the club captain, was left on the bench for the entire match after his public criticism of Carrick’s tactics in midweek, adding another layer to the sense of disconnect around the team. The reaction from high-profile observers was blunt. Gary Neville said, Source: Sky Sports

item.title: Bayern's Eberl: We don't really understand what we've achieved
item.description: Bayern Munich's Michael Olise celebrates scoring his side's third goal with his teammates during the German Bundesliga soccer match between SC Freiburg and Bayern Munich at Europa-Park Stadium. (is associated with: «Bayern's Eberl: We don't really understand what we've achieved») Harry Langer/dpa Bayern Munich board member for sport Max Eberl said he doesn't think the people in the club "really understand what we've achieved this week" as the Bavarians overcame the collapse of coach Vincent Kompany and the additional absence of key players with a 3-1 triumph at Freiburg on Sunday. "I don't think we really understand what we've achieved this week with all the hurdles we've had to overcome. What the team and we as a group have done with the coaching staff is extraordinary," Eberl said. "The win means three points, but it was a bigger win than just three points. Obviously we've got problems at the moment, but we have our squad and are really happy." Kompany collapsed while watching a training session of Bayern's reserve team. He had been suffering from a virus in previous days but the reason for the collapse is not known. Other Bayern absentees in Freiburg apart from Kompany were Joshua Kimmich due to a family bereavement as well as Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala, Aleksandar Pavlović, Luis Díaz and Kim Minjae for injury reasons. "It was clear to everyone that this game marked the end of a very, very difficult week, both physically and mentally," goalkeeper Jonas Urbig said. Urbig deputized once again for Neuer and made a crucial save at the end of the game when Bayern were leading 2-1 to deny Freiburg the equalizer. With the three points, Bayern moved back into first place on goal difference over Borussia Dortmund ahead of the two sides' table-topper showdown on Saturday in Munich. "We have a good cohesion, everyone supports everyone, no matter how difficult the situation is and what each individual is going through. We stand together, not only this week, but especially this week," Urbig said.

item.title: Marseille’s Keyliane Abdallah relegated to reserves after Le Havre performance
item.description: Marseille’s Keyliane Abdallah relegated to reserves after Le Havre performance Keyliane Abdallah (20) made his breakthrough into the Olympique de Marseille first team earlier this season, benefiting from the financial situation at his formative club in order to assert himself in Bruno Genesio’s side. The fire sale and inability to recruit have offered opportunities to Minots . Abdallah has, by and large, seized that chance. However, his entrance, as well as those of Neal Maupay, Angel Gomes, and Nouhoum Kamissoko, coincided with Marseille’s capitulation. Maupay and Abdallah came on just after Le Havre AC’s goal, which reduced the deficit to 4-1. Le HAC would go on to score two more. They also had two strong penalty shouts in stoppage time, one of which saw Clément Turpin go to the monitor before maintaining his decision. Bruno Genesio was left fuming. “I am very angry. If, around them, they are made to believe in great things, I am going to make sure that they rediscover humility,” the OM manager told Ligue 1 Plus. La Provence now understands that, in the wake of the slender 4-3 win over Le Havre, Abdallah has been relegated to the reserve side. He will remain there until further notice. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Sophie Cunningham turns heads as chequered flag waver at Formula 1’s United States GP
item.description: Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images WNBA free agent Sophie Cunningham appeared at Formula 1’s 2026 United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, as the chequered flag-waver. Cunningham has been surging in popularity over the last few months, gaining visibility as Caitlin Clark’s teammate on the Indiana Fever before her staunch political views on trans athletes in the WNBA made her a national figure. After appearing at NASCAR races throughout the season, Cunningham made her first appearance at a Formula 1 event to continue building on her off-court passion for motorsports. Sophie Cunningham’s appearance at F1 draws mixed reactions Cunningham was seen on the broadcast waving the chequered flag at the end of the race as the winner, Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes, came through first. F1 and WNBA fans were not expecting to see Cunningham on the broadcast in that role, and had mixed reactions to the same. “Sophie Cunningham waving the flag in Formula 1? What has happened to my beautiful sport?” said one disappointed fan . “Go Sophie!” said one fan who was excited to see the 30-year-old WNBA player at the race. “Sophie Cunningham waved the flag? W– are we doing? She’s not even a relevant basketball player. The shock about F1 isn’t that they are right-wing but my God, when they go low, it’s always in the sleaziest, cheapest way,” said one very angry fan . “Sophie Cunningham waved the chequered flag this afternoon at the F1 race in Austin. How cool is that? Antonelli is close to being World Champion at 20yo. What a talent!” said another fan who was excited to see Sophie’s appearance . “Of all the people to wave the chequered flag?!! F1 asked Sophie Cunningham?! When Paige Bueckers is right there?” said one Texas-based fan who was upset Sophie was asked instead of Dallas Wings star Paige Bueckers. “F1 race organisers are so gross for selecting Sophie Cunningham to wave the chequered flag. Why is everything in America about politics and gaining political points? So unnecessary,” were the harsh thoughts of another fan . Cunningham averaged 7.9 points in the WNBA last season. She is currently a free agent and is expected to decide on her next WNBA destination in a few months. item.title: Bundesliga Team of the Week – Matchday 7
item.description: Bundesliga Team of the Week – Matchday 7 With Matchday 7 of the 2026/27 Bundesliga season in the books, Bulinews Editor-in-Chief Rune Gjerulff has selected his Team of the Week, opting for an attack-minded 4-1-3-2 formation. Goalkeeper: Gregor Kobel, Borussia Dortmund Made several impressive saves to help Borussia Dortmund secure a clean sheet and a narrow 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt. Defenders: Anthony Caci, Mainz Continued his impressive form for Mainz, contributing a goal and an assist, but his efforts weren't enough to earn his side a point, as Die Nullfünfer fell to a 2-3 defeat against Werder Bremen. Dayot Upamecano, FC Bayern Upamecano made his presence felt at both ends of the pitch, finding the net with a well-timed forward run while winning seven duels and completing 94 percent of his passes. Ramy Bensebaini, Borussia Dortmund The Algeria international delivered a solid performance at the back, winning eight duels and completing 78 percent of his passes. Nathaniel Brown, FC Bayern Impressed going forward in FC Bayern's 3-1 win over Freiburg, providing an assist and registering two shots as he made his presence felt in attack. Midfielders: Han-Noah Massengo, Augsburg Delivered an excellent performance, scoring Augsburg's only goal against Union Berlin, while also completing 90 percent of his passes and winning all of his ground duels. Michael Olise, FC Bayern Olise was once again instrumental for FC Bayern, assisting Dayot Upamecano's opener before getting on the scoresheet himself to seal the 3-1 win over Freiburg. The Frenchman created five key chances and completed two dribbles in an influential performance. Andrej Kramaric, Hoffenheim Made a huge impact off the bench, playing a part in all three of Hoffenheim's goals against Leverkusen. He scored once and provided two assists to inspire his side's attacking display. Wael Mohya, Borussia Mönchengladbach The youngster was instrumental in Gladbach's first win of the season, scoring a goal and providing an assist to inspire his side to a 3-2 upset victory over VfB Stuttgart. Strikers: Niclas Füllkrug, Werder Bremen Scored twice from the penalty spot to take his tally to eight Bundesliga goals, moving clear at the top of the scoring charts. Romulo, RB Leipzig Introduced at half-time, Romulo provided an immediate spark for RB Leipzig, scoring twice in an impressive 4-0 victory over Elversberg. He also completed two dribbles to cap an influential cameo.

item.title: Hansi Flick plans Barcelona reset after PSG and Real Madrid defeats deepen injury crisis
item.description: Hansi Flick plans Barcelona reset after PSG and Real Madrid defeats deepen injury crisis Barcelona manager Hansi Flick wants his players to recover physically and mentally after consecutive defeats against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, according to a report from SPORT . Rather than immediately launching into an intensive tactical review, the German coach is prioritising rest, nutrition and a chance to disconnect before Barcelona resume their work on the training ground. The outlet mentions that Flick gathered his players shortly after the El Clasico defeat and believes restoring their freshness is the first step towards getting Barcelona back on track. However, the club’s growing injury problems, particularly in defence, continue to complicate his plans. Flick prioritises rest before Barcelona tactical review Notably, Flick has instructed his players to follow their dietary guidelines carefully and make the most of the opportunity to switch off from football. The Barcelona manager believes the squad needs a proper reset after a difficult spell that has included defeats against PSG and Real Madrid. Xavi Espart was injured against Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The plan also extends to Flick and his coaching staff, who are expected to benefit from stepping away from the immediate pressure before turning their attention to the team’s shortcomings. The Ballon d’Or ceremony presents a slight complication, as Lamine Yamal, Joan Garcia and Rodri are expected to travel , and Flick hopes they will also be able to disconnect from the demands surrounding the team before returning refreshed. From Wednesday onwards, the focus is expected to shift towards detailed discussions about Barcelona’s tactical organisation and on-pitch performances. Barcelona injury crisis leaves Flick short of defensive options Finding solutions to Barcelona’s injury problems is proving more difficult. This is because Flick believes many injuries, including the latest setback involving Xavi Espart , have resulted from physical knocks rather than inadequate preparation. That is crucial because it limits how much the coaching staff can realistically prevent through training adjustments alone. Flick is running short of options in defence. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The defensive department has been particularly affected, leaving Flick with fewer established options as Barcelona attempt to recover from their recent defeats. The manager has already acknowledged publicly that the squad’s available choices in those positions are limited. La Masia youngsters could receive more opportunities Barcelona’s academy is therefore becoming increasingly important as Flick manages the injury situation. Against Real Madrid, centre-back Alex Campos featured, while Orien Goren, a midfielder, was also involved amid Dani Olmo’s absence. item.content:encoded: Hansi Flick plans Barcelona reset after PSG and Real Madrid defeats deepen injury crisis Barcelona manager Hansi Flick wants his players to recover physically and mentally after consecutive defeats against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, according to a report from SPORT . Rather than immediately launching into an intensive tactical review, the German coach is prioritising rest, nutrition and a chance to disconnect before Barcelona resume their work on the training ground. The outlet mentions that Flick gathered his players shortly after the El Clasico defeat and believes restoring their freshness is the first step towards getting Barcelona back on track. However, the club’s growing injury problems, particularly in defence, continue to complicate his plans. Flick prioritises rest before Barcelona tactical review Notably, Flick has instructed his players to follow their dietary guidelines carefully and make the most of the opportunity to switch off from football. The Barcelona manager believes the squad needs a proper reset after a difficult spell that has included defeats against PSG and Real Madrid. Xavi Espart was injured against Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The plan also extends to Flick and his coaching staff, who are expected to benefit from stepping away from the immediate pressure before turning their attention to the team’s shortcomings. The Ballon d’Or ceremony presents a slight complication, as Lamine Yamal, Joan Garcia and Rodri are expected to travel , and Flick hopes they will also be able to disconnect from the demands surrounding the team before returning refreshed. From Wednesday onwards, the focus is expected to shift towards detailed discussions about Barcelona’s tactical organisation and on-pitch performances. Barcelona injury crisis leaves Flick short of defensive options Finding solutions to Barcelona’s injury problems is proving more difficult. This is because Flick believes many injuries, including the latest setback involving Xavi Espart , have resulted from physical knocks rather than inadequate preparation. That is crucial because it limits how much the coaching staff can realistically prevent through training adjustments alone. Flick is running short of options in defence. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The defensive department has been particularly affected, leaving Flick with fewer established options as Barcelona attempt to recover from their recent defeats. The manager has already acknowledged publicly that the squad’s available choices in those positions are limited. La Masia youngsters could receive more opportunities Barcelona’s academy is therefore becoming increasingly important as Flick manages the injury situation. Against Real Madrid, centre-back Alex Campos featured, while Orien Goren, a midfielder, was also involved amid Dani Olmo’s absence. Further opportunities for La Masia players could follow this week as Barcelona look to go through their depleted squad. Flick’s priority is to restore the team’s physical and mental sharpness before making tactical adjustments. But with injuries continuing to restrict his defensive options, the manager will have to find a way to work with a relatively short squad.

item.title: Real Madrid hero Andriy Lunin reveals the key to 2-1 win over Barcelona: ‘Discipline and attitude’
item.description: Real Madrid hero Andriy Lunin reveals the key to 2-1 win over Barcelona: ‘Discipline and attitude’ Andriy Lunin played a decisive role in Real Madrid’s 2-1 victory over Barcelona at Camp Nou on Sunday, producing a spectacular save to deny Gerard Martin in the 66th minute. The goalkeeper subsequently highlighted the discipline, determination and collective effort behind the victory, as Real Madrid extended their winning run to five consecutive matches. With Barcelona enjoying more possession, Lunin believes his side’s ability to remain organised and withstand pressure proved crucial in securing three important points in El Clasico. Lunin identifies discipline and determination as keys to victory Real Madrid had to work hard to protect their advantage against Barcelona, with Lunin producing a standout moment shortly after the hour mark. The goalkeeper stressed that winning away from home against a major rival required more than technical quality, pointing to the mentality his teammates displayed throughout the contest. “Discipline and attitude were key because Barcelona had more possession. “Determination was important too, because playing away is tough, and these three points were vital today because we all know how things stood.” Andriy Lunin was fantastic against Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Lunin also explained the importance of staying united when the match became difficult, explaining how Real Madrid adapted to Barcelona’s pressure rather than relying solely on their ability to dominate possession. “Our team effort was crucial. When you can dominate, play well and try to keep a clean sheet, you do so, but when the match gets tough – especially against big rivals like today’s – you have to know how to dig deep, manage the game and stay united as a team right until the end.” Lunin credits daily work for spectacular save Lunin’s reaction save to Gerard Martin’s header was one of the defining moments of the second half. The Ukrainian goalkeeper credited the work done in training for his ability to deliver when called upon, acknowledging the influence of goalkeeping coach Nuno. “Nuno (the goalkeeping coach) always says ‘well trained’, and I think that’s down to the daily work.” Lunin’s warning to Real Madrid Despite the significance of beating Barcelona, Lunin insisted Real Madrid must not allow their run of five consecutive victories to distract them from the work still required. item.description: What time is the World Series today? TV schedule, channel to watch Brewers vs. Rays games originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 World Series is set, with the best of the American League ready to take on the best of the National League. The Milwaukee Brewers finally won the NL pennant, making the World Series for the first time in 44 years after a franchise-best 103 wins in the regular season. Led by manager Pat Murphy, the Brewers have a very balanced team with stars like Jackson Chourio and Jacob Misiorowski ready to take the big stage. However, the Brewers will have to go through the Tampa Bay Rays , another team looking for its first-ever World Series championship. Kevin Cash's team is headlined by Junior Caminero, Yandy Diaz and Drew Rasmussen and won 98 games in the regular season. Milwaukee will have home-field advantage, but both these fan bases are excited for a potentially franchise-altering series. The Sporting News has you covered on all you need to know about how to watch and listen to every game of the World Series. What time is the World Series today? Fans looking for a streaming option can use DIRECTV or Fubo . Fubo offers a free trial for new subscribers, so you can try the service before you buy. Stream ESPN, ABC, CBS, Fox, NBC and 100+ top channels of live TV and sports without cable. (Participating plans only. Taxes and fees may apply.) item.title: World Series radio station 2026: Channel, streaming, schedule to listen live to Brewers vs. Rays broadcast
item.description: World Series radio station 2026: Channel, streaming, schedule to listen live to Brewers vs. Rays broadcast originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . More than a century after the first World Series radio broadcast, baseball remains the sport with the closest tie to the medium. Even if everyone has a screen in their pocket these days, it's not always possible to watch every pitch, and those who want to keep up with the action while driving, walking the dog, or just sitting on the porch can still tune in to the play-by-play. One of the best parts about listening to the World Series is the option to hear each team's home broadcasters, which is not an option for television viewers. But fans around the country can tune in as Andy Freed calls his third World Series in 22 seasons with the Rays, or get the Brewers angle from the legendary Bob Uecker's successors, Jeff Levering and Lane Grindle. Here's all you need to know to listen to Fall Classic games live. World Series radio station 2026 National radio station: SiriusXM app and channels 80, 202, 203 Local radio stations: 620 WTMJ (Milwaukee), Listen to live play-by-play coverage of every World Series game nationwide on the SiriusXM app, or in your vehicle on channels 80 (national broadcast), 202 (Rays call) and 203 (Brewers call). See the game-by-game schedule below. The SiriusXM Sports Pass allows fans to listen to live game broadcasts of the NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL, college football and basketball, the PGA Tour, NASCAR and more. Get your first month of the SiriusXM Sports Pass for free , then pay just $5 a month or $49 for a year. World Series radio announcers 2026 National: ESPN Radio has the national broadcast, with the same announcing crew returning for a fourth World Series together. Jon "Boog" Sciambi is on play-by-play with analysis from Eduardo Perez and Jessica Mendoza, and Buster Olney will handle reporting duties. Listen to the ESPN Radio broadcast on SiriusXM channel 80 . Brewers: Milwaukee's regular crew of Jeff Levering and Lane Grindle will have the call, with Josh Maurer also contributing to the broadcast. Listen to the Brewers' radio team on SiriusXM channel 203 . Rays: Longtime radio voice Andy Freed will have the call for Tampa Bay fans alongside Neil Solondz. Listen to the Rays' broadcast on SiriusXM channel 202 . World Series schedule 2026 Listen to every game live with SiriusXM . Date Game Time (ET) Fri., Oct. 23 Game 1 at Milwaukee 8 p.m. Sat., Oct. 24 Game 2 at Milwaukee 8 p.m. Mon., Oct. 26 Game 3 at Tampa Bay 8 p.m. Tue., Oct. 27 Game 4 at Tampa Bay 8 p.m. Wed., Oct. 28 Game 5 at Tampa Bay* 8 p.m. Fri., Oct. 30 Game 6 at Milwaukee* 8 p.m. Sat., Oct. 31 Game 7 at Milwaukee* 8 p.m. * If necessary MLB playoffs bracket 2026 SN Related Links Latest MLB news and rumors 2026 MLB schedule and scores MLB standings 2026 How to bet on MLB

item.title: Florian Wirtz injury: What Andoni Iraola said after 23y/o hobbled off during Liverpool win
item.description: Florian Wirtz injury: What Andoni Iraola said after 23y/o hobbled off during Liverpool win Liverpool’s 2-0 win over Brighton on Sunday was tempered by an injury to Florian Wirtz just before the midway point of the second half. The 23-year-old required treatment on the pitch and was substituted for Trey Nyoni in the 65th minute with a suspected ankle problem. It was the German’s shot that Pascal Gross diverted into his team’s net for the Reds’ opening goal in the first half, with our number 7 enjoying another influential performance before he was forced off later in the afternoon. What did Iraola say on Wirtz injury? After the match, Andoni Iraola provided an update on the injury to Wirtz, with the head coach confident that it’s not a major issue but also preaching caution given the tight turnaround between fixtures. The Basque said (via liverpoolfc.com ): “Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle. It doesn’t look very big but we are playing every three days, so we need to see where he is. “ (Photo by Jan Kruger/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Hopefully Wirtz will be OK to face Arsenal With Iraola likely to shuffle the pack for the Carabao Cup tie against Chelsea on Wednesday, it’d make little sense to play Wirtz so soon after twisting his ankle. Even had he not been injured yesterday, we suspect he’d have been one of those removed from the starting XI in midweek. It’d be much more beneficial to look towards next weekend’s huge Premier League showdown against Arsenal as a potential return date for the 23-year-old, in the hope that the problem will have subsided by then. The German had been much maligned by the wider public over the past few months but has been enjoying some strong performances in recent games, with Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle hailing an ‘excellent’ display against Villarreal last week (in which he scored). The same journalist praised Wirtz’s efforts before going off against Brighton yesterday, writing that our nmber 7 was ‘dangerous whenever in possession, found good pockets [and] used [the] ball well’ ( Liverpool Echo ), in additon to bringing about the first goal. Fingers crossed for good news on the ex-Bayer Leverkusen man over the coming days, and that he’ll be cleared to play when Arsenal rumble into town next Sunday.

item.title: Nico Carrillo Defends Featherweight Muay Thai World Title Against Nabil Anane In Rematch At The Inner Circle 43
item.description: “King of the North” Nico Carrillo ’s first assignment as undisputed ONE Featherweight Muay Thai World Champion is confirmed, and it brings a familiar name back into his path. The Scottish knockout machine will defend his coveted gold in a rematch against Algerian-Thai slugger Nabil Anane at The Inner Circle 43 inside Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, December 18, with the action available to subscribers at live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram Their long-awaited sequel joins the previously announced ONE Strawweight Muay Thai World Title unification bout between reigning king Prajanchai Pongsuphan PK and interim titleholder Aliff Sor Dechapan . When Carrillo and Anane last met at ONE 170 in January 2025, the Glaswegian arrived on a 15-fight winning streak and with a reputation as one of the sport’s most feared strikers. That night did not go his way, though, as Anane finished him in the first round to claim the ONE Interim Bantamweight Muay Thai World Championship. Since then, “King of the North” has moved up to featherweight and chalked up another remarkable 4-0 run in the world’s largest martial arts organization. He earned back-to-back finishes of Sitthichai Sitsongpeenong and Luke “The Chef” Lessei to book a shot at the interim crown against Shadow Mavinn at ONE Fight Night 40 this past February. Photo Credit: ONE Championship That evening, the Deachkalek Muay Thai Academy representative delivered a strong five-round performance to walk away with 26 pounds of gold . He was then elevated to undisputed ONE Featherweight Muay Thai World Champion in July, when Tawanchai PK Saenchai vacated the title. In August, Carrillo took a massive step toward becoming a two-sport ONE World Champion when he opened his promotional kickboxing account with a second-round knockout of Zhou “Qilin” Jiaqiang at ONE Fight Night 46 . Waiting at The Inner Circle 43 is the man who made that first meeting the biggest night of his young career. View this post on Instagram Anane was only 20 when he stunned “King of the North” inside Bangkok’s Impact Arena. He floored the Scotsman three times en route to a sixth straight triumph on the global stage. From there, he outpointed “The Kicking Machine” Superlek , was later elevated to undisputed ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion, then ventured into two kickboxing battles, which included a win over Hiromi “The Purple Comet” Wajima at ONE 173 in Tokyo, Japan. The ride has had its bumps, however. Rambolek Chor Ajalaboon took his gold in a five-round battle at The Inner Circle 7 , and Suakim Pongsuphan PK edged him by split decision this past August. He has since returned to winning ways with a unanimous decision win over former K-1 Champion Yuki Yoza at ONE SAMURAI 4 in a bantamweight kickboxing tiff earlier this month. item.title: Lyon predicted XI v PSG: Keito Nakamura suspended, Pavel Sulc out
item.description: Lyon predicted XI v PSG: Keito Nakamura suspended, Pavel Sulc out Olympique Lyonnais’ forward options are severely limited as they head to the Parc des Princes to face Paris Saint-Germain on Monday night. This game has been rearranged. It was initially scheduled to take place on Sunday night, but the ongoing protests across the country saw the Paris Prefecture issue a directive for it to be postponed. Lyon are without several key attackers. Lois Openda is still out for several weeks after sustaining an injury against RC Lens. Pavel Sulc, meanwhile, suffered a meniscus injury in training this week and will be out until the New Year. Keito Nakamura, meanwhile, is suspended for the encounter. It may be Khalis Merah who starts as a false No.9, whilst Rémi Hiimbert is also an option at Paulo Fonseca’s disposal. Lyon likely line-up v PSG Dominik Greif; Abner, Moussa Niakhaté, Felix Bacher, Zachary Akethame; Corentin Tolisso, Tyler Morton, Tanner Tessmann; Julien Duranville, Khalis Merah, Ernest Nuamah. (L’Éq) GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Is there a World Series game today? Full TV schedule, times, channels for Brewers vs. Rays Game 3
item.description: Is there a World Series game today? Full TV schedule, times, channels for Brewers vs. Rays Game 3 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a pair of agonizing losses in Milwaukee, the Rays will look to turn the World Series around as they return to Florida for Game 3. The Brewers rallied from a 4-0 first-inning deficit in Game 2, chipping away at the Tampa Bay pitching staff while their bullpen put up six scoreless innings before Cooper Pratt singled in the go-ahead run in the seventh for a 5-4 win. The Rays will hope a return to Tropicana Field, where their 55-26 record during the regular season matched Milwaukee's for MLB's best mark at home, helps get them back on track. It will be the first World Series game at the Trop since Oct. 23, 2008, when the Rays picked up their lone win of that five-game series loss to the Phillies. Better yet for Tampa Bay, Freddy Peralta will get the start on the heels of earning MVP honors in the ALCS. The Rays will need another shutdown performance from him along with more consistent production from their lineup to get back in the series. Here's everything you need to know about Game 3 of the World Series, including TV channel and streaming options for Rays vs. Brewers. When is the next World Series game? Date : Monday, Oct. 26 Time : 8 p.m. ET | 7 p.m. CT After a travel day Sunday, Game 3 of the World Series between the Rays and Brewers is scheduled to begin Monday at 8 p.m. from Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. Where to watch Rays vs. Brewers Game 3 TV channels: Fox Live streams: Fubo Fox will have coverage of Game 3 of the World Series, with Joe Davis and John Smoltz set to call the game. item.title: MLB playoff schedule 2026: Full bracket, scores, times, TV channels to watch every postseason series
item.description: MLB playoff schedule 2026: Full bracket, scores, times, TV channels to watch every postseason series originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . More than seven months after pitchers and catchers reported to spring training, it's time to determine which team will wear the MLB crown in 2026. Twelve teams reached the postseason bracket, and the last two standing are the teams with the best records in their respective leagues during the regular season. Neither the Brewers nor the Rays has won a World Series, with Milwaukee's last appearance coming way back in 1982 and Tampa Bay falling short in 2020 and 2008. Who will survive the gauntlet to lift the Commissioner's Trophy at the end of October? Here's when and where to watch every game. Where to watch MLB playoffs 2026 TV channels: Fox, FS1, TBS, NBC, NBCSN Live streams: DIRECTV , Fubo , Peacock The 2026 MLB postseason will have a new look for the opening round, with NBC carrying every wild card game on its platforms: NBC, NBCSN and/or Peacock . After that, the familiar rotation returns. This year's NL playoffs will air on Fox or FS1 while the AL will be on TBS, with the World Series set to air on Fox as it has every year since 2000. Fans can stream every postseason game except Peacock exclusives with DIRECTV , which offers a free trial to new subscribers. All games airing on NBC, NBCSN, Fox and FS1 can be streamed with Fubo , which also offers a free trial. item.title: Backstage Update On Rusev's WWE Future (WWE News)
item.description: WWE.com Having not been seen on WWE programming for three months, there's now an update on the status of Rusev . The Bulgarian Brute was last in televised action on the 27th July episode of Raw, where he lost to Je'Von Evans. However, it appears that a return could be on the horizon for the former United States Champion . Via Fightful Select , discussions have been ongoing since September when it comes to Rusev's return to TV, and he's been training in-ring for that return, too. So, it sounds as if we might be seeing Rusev back on our screens sooner rather than later. While Rusev hasn't wrestled on TV for three months, he did return to action at a couple of Hawaii house shows earlier this month, losing to Joe Hendry on October 16th, then teaming with Ethan Page in a loss to Chad Gable and Rey Fenix the following day. Of course, Rusev returned to WWE shortly after WrestleMania 41, having spent the previous five years with AEW . Fair to say, it's been somewhat of a stop-start second stint with WWE for the 40-year-old, likely highlighted by a fun feud with Sheamus and an on-off alliance with Ethan Page. That aforementioned July Raw match against Je'Von Evans saw Rusev land awkwardly and suffer temporary numbness in his hands, as later confirmed by his wife, CJ Perry . Thankfully, Ru-Ru has since been able to return to the ring at those Honolulu, Hawaii live events, and it now remains to be seen as and when he returns to TV, and also whether he'll once again pick up that tag team with All Ego. item.title: ‘No One Cares,’ ‘Bright Spot in a Dismal Game’ — NFL Fans React as Chiefs’ Travis Kelce Sets TE Milestone in Embarrassing Loss
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) walks off the field after a loss against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. © Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Travis Kelce made history on a night that gave the Kansas City Chiefs little else to celebrate. The three-time Super Bowl champion caught four passes for 44 yards on eight targets in Sunday night’s 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. That was enough to pass Tony Gonzalez for the most receiving yards by a tight end in NFL history, playoffs included. The milestone came on National Tight Ends Day, of all days. Kansas City never reached the end zone, though, and fans who reacted to the record also reacted to the score. NFL Fans React as Travis Kelce Surpasses Tony Gonzalez’ TE Record Kelce went into the night needing 35 yards to pass Gonzalez, whose 15,413 career receiving yards included 15,127 in the regular season and 286 in the playoffs. The 37-year-old began Week 7 with 15,379 yards of his own, 13,301 in the regular season and 2,078 in the postseason. Notably, playoff yards made the difference, since Kelce started the night 1,826 regular-season yards behind Gonzalez. Kelce played in 25 playoff games through his first 13 seasons, while Gonzalez played in seven. Kelce passed him on his third catch of the night, with Kansas City down by double digits in the fourth quarter. He finished with 15,423 combined yards, 10 more than Gonzalez. Several fans who took notice of Kelce’s feat were proud of the star tight end and frustrated with the rest of the night. One fan wrote, “Bright spot in a dismal game!” Another fan agreed: “That’s the only good to come out this game.” Kansas City finished with 213 total yards and 11 first downs, went 3-of-11 on third down, ran for 50 yards on 16 carries, and never got into the red zone. Wish we had a better showing.” For this fan, the milestone came with a catch: “He’s the GOAT, but he’d rather just win the game.” Not everyone was in the mood to celebrate. item.title: In Ohio State return, Thad Matta lauds JJ Sullinger kidney donation to Terence Dials
item.description: Over 21 years, mostly at Ohio State , former Buckeyes coach Thad Matta accumulated 502 career wins, reached two Final Fours and one national championship game. He won a bunch of regular-season and conference tournament titles. But when Matta talks about his time as a coach, he doesn't focus on his accomplishments. So, it was no surprise that he used a ceremony honoring him on Oct. 25 to laud two of his former players instead. “Maybe the greatest thing I’ve seen in my coaching career happened a few weeks ago,” Matta told the crowd during halftime of OSU’s exhibition game against Butler . “A few weeks ago, James (J.J.) Sullinger gave his kidney to his teammate, Terence Dials .” Standing off to Matta’s left at the Schottenstein Center, Sullinger was embraced by Barbara Matta, Thad’s wife, while Sullinger struggled to hold in his emotions. A Central Ohio product, Sullinger played his freshman season at Arkansas in 2001-02 before transferring back to Ohio State, sitting out the next year to satisfy the rules of the time and then playing for the Buckeyes for three seasons. For all four years Sullinger was at Ohio State, Dials was his teammate. Dials, who is now on staff as coach Jake Diebler’s recruiting coordinator, underwent the procedure Oct. 12 and is making steady progress in his recovery. After hugging Matta’s wife, Sullinger was embraced by his former coach whose Ohio State tenure began in 2004-05 and lasted for 13 seasons. “That is what coaching is about, building the friendships and the trust these guys have,” Matta said. “College basketball has changed. I don’t know if these current players are ever going to get to experience what these guys had – the camaraderie and all the great moments that we shared.” More: Ohio State's John Mobley Jr. says he rolled his ankle against Butler Matta’s recognition featured a video showcasing former players sending their best wishes. Then Matta was presented with a commemorative basketball celebrating his career. For about three minutes, he spoke to the Ohio State crowd. “I’ve been wanting to say this: O-H,” he said, prompting the announced crowd of 6,996 to reply, “I-O.” Matta took in the game from almost the exact same vantage point as he did while leading the Buckeyes. He sat in the courtside seating that has been installed at the arena since his departure and was right next to the Ohio State bench with a good view of his former staff member Jake Diebler, who is now head coach for the Buckeyes. “It’s funny how many times I saw myself in him with what he was doing and what he was saying,” Matta told The Dispatch after Ohio State’s 82-73 win. “It was special to sit in those seats.” Diebler has been pushing for years for Matta to return to the program. item.content:encoded: Over 21 years, mostly at Ohio State , former Buckeyes coach Thad Matta accumulated 502 career wins, reached two Final Fours and one national championship game. He won a bunch of regular-season and conference tournament titles. But when Matta talks about his time as a coach, he doesn't focus on his accomplishments. So, it was no surprise that he used a ceremony honoring him on Oct. 25 to laud two of his former players instead. “Maybe the greatest thing I’ve seen in my coaching career happened a few weeks ago,” Matta told the crowd during halftime of OSU’s exhibition game against Butler . “A few weeks ago, James (J.J.) Sullinger gave his kidney to his teammate, Terence Dials .” Standing off to Matta’s left at the Schottenstein Center, Sullinger was embraced by Barbara Matta, Thad’s wife, while Sullinger struggled to hold in his emotions. A Central Ohio product, Sullinger played his freshman season at Arkansas in 2001-02 before transferring back to Ohio State, sitting out the next year to satisfy the rules of the time and then playing for the Buckeyes for three seasons. For all four years Sullinger was at Ohio State, Dials was his teammate. Dials, who is now on staff as coach Jake Diebler’s recruiting coordinator, underwent the procedure Oct. 12 and is making steady progress in his recovery. After hugging Matta’s wife, Sullinger was embraced by his former coach whose Ohio State tenure began in 2004-05 and lasted for 13 seasons. “That is what coaching is about, building the friendships and the trust these guys have,” Matta said. “College basketball has changed. I don’t know if these current players are ever going to get to experience what these guys had – the camaraderie and all the great moments that we shared.” More: Ohio State's John Mobley Jr. says he rolled his ankle against Butler Matta’s recognition featured a video showcasing former players sending their best wishes. Then Matta was presented with a commemorative basketball celebrating his career. For about three minutes, he spoke to the Ohio State crowd. “I’ve been wanting to say this: O-H,” he said, prompting the announced crowd of 6,996 to reply, “I-O.” Matta took in the game from almost the exact same vantage point as he did while leading the Buckeyes. He sat in the courtside seating that has been installed at the arena since his departure and was right next to the Ohio State bench with a good view of his former staff member Jake Diebler, who is now head coach for the Buckeyes. “It’s funny how many times I saw myself in him with what he was doing and what he was saying,” Matta told The Dispatch after Ohio State’s 82-73 win. “It was special to sit in those seats.” Diebler has been pushing for years for Matta to return to the program. After Matta retired following the 2025-26 season, Diebler invited Matta to visit campus during the summer for Ohio State’s annual “Vet Week,” which is when former players come back to work out and spend time with the current team. Matta wound up staying for two days. When the Buckeyes scheduled the Bulldogs, the other program Matta is most closely associated with, they decided it made sense to honor him as well. “It’s always amazing to come back in here,” Matta said. “You start to go through your mind all the incredible memories and moments that I was able to enjoy here. Columbus, 13 years, this is home. We raised our kids here. It was special for myself and our family.” After the game ended, a group of former players stuck around to spend time on the floor with Matta and his family. At least half an hour after the last fans had filed their way out, many of the former Buckeyes were still there holding court with the former coach. “I’m so proud of what we built here and how we built it, probably most importantly,” he said. “One thing I’ve learned about coaching: When you’re done, everybody forgets. Nobody cares. From that perspective, it felt like coming home today. Walking into the arena and sitting in the seats where I coached for 13 years was really special.” Sitting there, watching Ohio State and Butler play, Matta said he realized that he knew he was right in his decision to retire so that he could enjoying “coming to a game like this and hoping both teams play well.” It also meant he could take the time to celebrate two special teammates amid a group of former Buckeyes. “I’m humbled to say 502 wins,” he said. “I never scored a point, I never got a rebound. It’s these guys right here behind me.” Ohio State men's basketball beat writer Adam Jardy can be reached at ajardy@dispatch.com , on Bluesky at @ cdadamjardy.bsky.social , on Instagram at @ cdadamjardy or on Twitter at @ AdamJardy . This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: In Ohio State return, Thad Matta lauds JJ Sullinger kidney donation to Terence Dials

item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following loss to Pistons at home
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers took their first loss of the season on Sunday as they fell to the Detroit Pistons 106-93. The Sixers were unable to overcome the absence of Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe, and Jabari Walker in this one, but the Pistons were short-handed as well as they were missing All-Star big man Jalen Duren as well as elite defensive stopper Ausar Thompson. LeBron James returned from a 1-game absence and had 18 points and five assists for the Sixers while Tyrese Maxey had 29 points, five rebounds, and four assists. Jaylen Brown added 16 points, Dean Wade added seven and five rebounds, and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope had seven points, Adem Bona had six points, 13 rebounds, and three blocks off the bench. Here are the three biggest takeaways from the loss: The loss came down to the little things Of course, the Sixers are missing some key pieces when it comes to the rebounding struggles as Embiid, Walker, Dominick Barlow, and Tacko Fall are all sidelined. Any one of those four would help Philadelphia overcome a 54-37 rebounding deficit as the Pistons overwhelmed the Sixers on the glass a bit. Another big issue was free-throw shooting as the Sixers shot just 14-for-23 from the line. Brown shot just 4-for-8 from the line while James was just 2-for-6, and Maxey missed a critical free throw when Philadelphia was on the comeback trail. "I think, obviously, that never helps," coach Nick Nurse said of the free throw struggles. "But I think the rebounding was a huge factor. I think we executed offensively very well for stretches of the game. But we got off to a really slow start. That could probably – pin it on that. I thought we fought really, really hard from there. Once we started getting into the game, we fought really hard, but it just wasn't very pretty on three-point shooting, free-throw shooting and offensive execution." Brown has a tough night One has to give a ton of credit to Pistons wing Ron Holland II who hopped off the bench and made life miserable for Brown in this one. The star forward shot just 5-for-20 and was 2-for-6 from deep. He also committed five fouls and was just unable to convert on the looks. One has to wonder if that's just basketball as the game can be as simple as make or miss at times, or if Brown could have worked to find himself better looks within the offensive ecosystem. "I’ve got to look at it a little bit," acknowledged Nurse. "I think that – I think I talked about this the other night: I think when it comes out to him, I think there's some more vault-up-and-shoot threes. He obviously had a lot of traffic in there tonight. And I think he got to some good spots down there and just didn’t get them in there. A number of close-up finishes that normally would go. But I thought he was in a lot of traffic tonight." And he was able to stick one of them, which was a pretty big basket." This article originally appeared on Sixers Wire: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following loss to Pistons at home

item.title: College football NCAA Re-Rank 1-138 gets new look after Week 8 upsets
item.description: Brigham Young drops out of the top five but a Big 12 rival steps up to replace the Cougars in the USA TODAY Sports NCAA Re-Rank 1-138. Following losses by BYU and Texas Tech, Utah delivered a key win against Houston to rise to No. 4 in the new re-rank. One week after a huge win against Notre Dame, BYU fell three spots to No. 6 after losing to Central Florida. The drop was much bigger for the Red Raiders . A weak schedule plus a one-sided loss to Cincinnati dumps Tech down to No. 29, last among one-loss Power Four teams. Ohio State remains No. 1, followed by Miami. Georgia moved up one spot to No. 3 and Indiana climbed to No. 5 after an overtime win against Michigan. HIGHS AND LOWS: Week 8 winners and losers led by Big 12 flop Two SEC teams joined (or rejoined) the top 10 in No. 9 Kentucky and No. 10 Texas. The 7-1 Wildcats lead the SEC standings after beating Vanderbilt. The Longhorns rebounded from two losses in a row to take a must-have game against Ole Miss . The Rebels dropped to No. 12. Another unpredictable weekend led to double-digit drops for multiple Big Ten teams in No. 23 Iowa (down 11), No. 30 USC (down 15) and No. 39 Oregon (down 11). This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: College football NCAA Re-Rank 1-138 gets new look after Week 8 upsets

item.title: VOTE for the HSS North Jersey Football Team of the Week for Week 8
item.description: After an exciting Week 8 of the high school football season, it's time to look back on the top team performances. Read about the teams that stood out last week and let us know which one should be the HSS North Jersey Football Team of the Week in the poll at the bottom of this page. Voting closes at 5 p.m. Thursday, Oct. 29. Lakeland The Lancers (7-2) rallied from a 16-point deficit by scoring the final three TDs for a 39-36 victory over Dumont. Hunter Struble passed for 287 yards, with TD passes to Ryan Farris, Ryan Sabric and Chace Severs, and he ran for the game-winning, 8-yard score in the fourth. North Arlington The Vikings (3-5) secured their first shutout since 2024 with a 6-0 victory over Cresskill/Emerson. Julian Castanheira had 10 tackles and an interception and Ryan Kropp had 10 tackles. Nathan Castanheira threw for 245 yards, including a 20-yard score in the fourth to Jason Arocho. Pascack Hills The Broncos (7-1) won their SFC Ivy semifinal over Millburn in double-overtime, 21-14. Dane Brimigion threw for 106 yards, including a 29-yard score to Brady Frischer in the second extra session. Frischer and Jack Epstein each ran for second-half scores to help erase a 14-0 deficit. Rutherford The Bulldogs (8-1) continued to pile up points with a 42-35 victory over Butler. Myles Balchan passed for 324 yards and four TDs. Will Holman had seven catches for 183 yards and two scores, and AJ Nunziato and Russ Snyder also caught TDs. John Gioia ran for two scores. Secaucus The young Patriots (1-7) broke through with a 38-18 victory over Dunellen. Tonty Rutinel-Caraballo made nine tackles. Sean Donis and Sloan Bello had five tackles apiece and Aaron Tamang had four. Teipauli Iona made two tackles for losses, and Ethan Bruno had an interception. St. Joseph The Green Knights (4-4) played outstanding defense in a 10-7 win over rival Bergen Catholic. Tahj Gray, Ryan Barry and Jonathan Galette each had interceptions. William Mitchell threw for 172 yards, with a 42-yard score to Stalin Knowlden, and Kyle Salinas kicked a 41-yard field goal. Waldwick/Midland Park The Warriors (8-1) rallied past Garfield to win their first NJIC title, 35-34, in overtime. Luciano Mayer ran for three TDs, including one in OT, and Will Dell’Aglio and Aidan Maher each ran for a score to help erase a 21-7 deficit. On the final play, they stopped a 2-point conversion run. West Milford The Highlanders (2-7) delivered their most dominant performance of the season in a 28-7 win over Sparta. Luke Maslanek threw for 175 yards, with a 33-yard score to Blake Tyburczy, and he ran for three TDs. Colton Naccara had 13 tackles and Tyburczy had nine tackles and an interception. Vote! Note: If you can't see the poll, try refreshing the link or clearing the cache in your browser. If you are viewing the poll in the Twitter app, try viewing it in the Varsity Aces app or at NorthJersey.com. This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: VOTE for the HSS North Jersey Football Team of the Week

He followed that up with a strong 9-point, 11-rebound effort against the Dallas Mavericks . Pacers Head Coach Explains How Ivica Zubac Fits On The Team’s Offensive System Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – SEPTEMBER 28: Ivica Zubac #40 of the Indiana Pacers poses for a photo during media day at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on September 28, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle has a fast-paced system, something Ivica Zubac is not used to when he was still playing with the Los Angeles Lakers and the LA Clippers . According to Carlisle, the Pacers are adjusting to fit Zubac into their offensive system. “Our system is slightly different than what they did with the Clippers,” Carlisle said, “but he’s working hard at adjusting to how we play, and there’s certain things that we’re adjusting because he’s a little different than anybody we’ve ever had.” “You never are all the way to your destination. There’s always going to be work and adjustments and continued need for attention to detail, with everything, with Zu and everybody else we have.” His teammate Andrew Nembhard has also opened up on Zubac’s fit with the team, saying that the post-up big gave the team a new dynamic and they are looking to harness his potential alongside Tyrese Haliburton. “Just communicating what we see out there and understanding,” Nembhard said. “We’re just working on him getting up to touch. He’s always been in a drop. I think the biggest thing that he helps us with is the defensive rebounds and our defensive possessions, but start our offense too.” “It’s been like a year or so, so it’s just like creating that chemistry like I was talking about. A lot of guys can do a lot of different things out there, so just trying to be aggressive but also fit in at the same time,” he added. Zubac is considered a crucial piece for the Pacers this season, especially as the team is welcoming back Tyrese Haliburton, who sat out the entire season last year. item.title: Ansu Fati sustains thigh injury in Monaco draw
item.description: Ansu Fati sustains thigh injury in Monaco draw Ansu Fati missed the start of the season due to injury and he is now set for another spell on the sidelines. It is thought that the Spaniard sustained a thigh injury during the draw against Lille OSC on Sunday afternoon. The previous week, Fati started his first Ligue 1 game of the season. Whilst he started the match against SC Freiburg on Thursday from the bench, he came on in the second half and netted in a 3-0 win. He then made back-to-back starts in Ligue 1, starting in the No.10 position against LOSC at the Stade Louis II. However, he only managed 15 minutes before being forced off. He was replaced by Mathys Detourbet. It is thought that Fati has sustained a hamstring injury, the gravity of which has yet to be ascertained. Speaking post-match, Filipe Luís said that they had to be “careful” with the former Barcelona forward. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: ‘No light switch’ – Mike Brown gives ruthless reality check to Knicks after terrible start to season
item.description: Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images Mike Brown has delivered a blunt message to the New York Knicks after the defending NBA champions suffered their third consecutive defeat to open the new season. New York fell 111-102 to the Orlando Magic at Madison Square Garden, surrendering a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter as their early-season struggles continued. While Brown demanded greater accountability from his players, captain Jalen Brunson also addressed the team, urging his teammates to stay united through the difficult start. Mike Brown insists New York Knicks must improve after 0-3 start Brown made it clear that last season’s championship success would not excuse the Knicks’ current performances. Speaking after the defeat , the head coach said: “The biggest thing is to continue to coach them and/or tell them the truth.” He also warned that he would not tolerate a lack of effort, stressing the importance of practising the right habits and carrying them into games. However, his strongest words came when he explained why New York could not expect to turn things around simply by relying on their reputation as champions. Brown said: “If we’re trying and trying the right way, sometimes you got to fight through stuff like this to get yourself on track. But games like this will tell us that, like I said before, our c*** stinks. You know, it does. And we’re the only ones that can do something about it. There’s no light switch that we can just turn on and think we’re gonna go win ballgames.” The Knicks’ collapse against Orlando highlighted those concerns. They gave up 40 points late in the game and committed eight costly turnovers as the Magic took control. Brunson delivered a similar message to his teammates, although his approach was more measured. “Control what you can control; focus on the little details that may seem small but are going to impact winning. Most importantly, let’s do it together,” the Knicks captain said. New York have now lost to the Philadelphia 76ers, Boston Celtics and Magic, leaving them at 0-3 to begin their title defence. The Knicks still have time to recover, but Brown’s message is clear: last season’s success will count for little unless his players start delivering on the court. item.title: Crisis in SEC, Big Ten lead college football overreactions after Week 8
item.description: With the first two months of the college football season nearly completed, all we’ve really learned is that the race for the national championship is, well, pretty much as wide open as we expected it to be. We’ve already seen four different teams occupy the No. 1 spot in the US LBM Coaches Poll , but nobody seems truly safe on any given Saturday. Another busy weekend of action left us with plenty of observations, and as usual we’re here to try and sort out the overreactions from the legitimate conclusions about what we just witnessed. We begin once again in the conference of greater meaningfulness. Blame the nine-game schedule for SEC chaos A cursory glance at the SEC standings will tell you there are just two teams remaining with one league loss. One is Georgia, which you might have anticipated at the start of the campaign. The other is Kentucky, a development that is a surprise to everybody – with the possible exception of Will Stein himself. Furthermore, any attempt to sort the list of two-loss teams into some sort of logical order will send you down a set of tangled loops more confusing than suburban cul-de-sacs. PATH TO PLAYOFF: Sign up for our college football newsletter It’s easy to point to the addition of a ninth conference game to explain the lack of clarity at this juncture of the season, but that’s only part of the issue. The real culprit – and the SEC is not alone in this – is expansion. The power conferences went to a nine-game slate in part to address the imbalance of schedule strengths within the leagues. We might indeed achieve the intended separation over the final month, but there’s still considerable luck of the draw involved that could wind up determining who goes to the league championship game. This in turn brings us to another issue we’re going to encounter in future seasons when the playoff expansion nobody wants becomes reality. The elimination of conference championship weekend will remove a key datapoint from an already imperfect process. In large conferences with 16 to 18 members, teams are obviously going to miss playing nearly half the league, and one mechanism to bring the top two finishers together for what more often than not is an incredibly entertaining game will be gone. In short, bigger is often not better when it comes to both conference size and the postseason field. item.content:encoded: With the first two months of the college football season nearly completed, all we’ve really learned is that the race for the national championship is, well, pretty much as wide open as we expected it to be. We’ve already seen four different teams occupy the No. 1 spot in the US LBM Coaches Poll , but nobody seems truly safe on any given Saturday. Another busy weekend of action left us with plenty of observations, and as usual we’re here to try and sort out the overreactions from the legitimate conclusions about what we just witnessed. We begin once again in the conference of greater meaningfulness. Blame the nine-game schedule for SEC chaos A cursory glance at the SEC standings will tell you there are just two teams remaining with one league loss. One is Georgia, which you might have anticipated at the start of the campaign. The other is Kentucky, a development that is a surprise to everybody – with the possible exception of Will Stein himself. Furthermore, any attempt to sort the list of two-loss teams into some sort of logical order will send you down a set of tangled loops more confusing than suburban cul-de-sacs. PATH TO PLAYOFF: Sign up for our college football newsletter It’s easy to point to the addition of a ninth conference game to explain the lack of clarity at this juncture of the season, but that’s only part of the issue. The real culprit – and the SEC is not alone in this – is expansion. The power conferences went to a nine-game slate in part to address the imbalance of schedule strengths within the leagues. We might indeed achieve the intended separation over the final month, but there’s still considerable luck of the draw involved that could wind up determining who goes to the league championship game. This in turn brings us to another issue we’re going to encounter in future seasons when the playoff expansion nobody wants becomes reality. The elimination of conference championship weekend will remove a key datapoint from an already imperfect process. In large conferences with 16 to 18 members, teams are obviously going to miss playing nearly half the league, and one mechanism to bring the top two finishers together for what more often than not is an incredibly entertaining game will be gone. In short, bigger is often not better when it comes to both conference size and the postseason field. Big Ten offenses are all broken You’d be forgiven if you peeked at the Big Ten scoreboard this weekend and believed you’d been transported back to the 1970’s. There were final scores of 13-10, 13-6 – and that one went overtime – and three other results in which the losing team managed 10 points or fewer. We expect scores like that in games involving Iowa, of course, but even Indiana, which averaged 41.6 points a game during its championship run last season, has scored just a total of 43 points in its last three outings. So what gives? Can nobody play offense anymore? As with many such questions, there is not one simple answer. In the case of the Hoosiers, a Heisman caliber quarterback can’t just be plugged in, despite how easy it might have looked last year. Injuries have factored into it as well at several league locales, and coaching staff changes as well as the usual player turnover have also contributed to defenses being ahead of offenses even at this late stage of the season. At this point, however, these teams probably are who they are, so don’t expect the Big Ten to start putting up video-game numbers the rest of the way. And oh yeah, did we mention a certain individual award denoted by an iconic statuette? A non-quarterback will win the Heisman Given all the subpar QB play we’ve seen – and it’s not just the Big Ten –, it seems like conditions are favorable for a player at a different position to bring home the hardware this year. Who might that be though? The obvious candidate, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith, will be working with a backup passer for the foreseeable future with Julian Sayin sidelined with a shoulder injury. Miami standout receiver Malachi Toney has a strong argument, but he and his own quarterback Darian Mensah might split votes. For a lengthy part of its history the Heisman was a running back award, but no ball carriers have distinguished themselves with eye-popping numbers this season. In truth, the race seems as wide open as the playoff hunt, which should make for a lot of intrigue in the season’s final month. Big 12 parity should get more respect While SEC teams were picking each other off through the first seven weeks, the Big 12 leaders had avoided cannibalizing themselves. All that changed in Week 8, however, as two of the league’s three unbeaten teams lost on the road. Unfortunately, as the committee has demonstrated in past years, parity in the Big 12 does not lead to multiple invitations as it does in the SEC or Big Ten . A road loss at Cincinnati or Central Florida is more damaging than a loss to, say, Ohio State or Florida. That’s – just reality. Now having said that, there are results in those conferences as well that would qualify as resume eliminators – Oregon, anyone? –, but like it or not, there’s less margin for error in the Big 12 because of the lack of head-to-head non-conference wins. Boise State is a lock for the College Football Playoff Still the lone team from the so-called Group of Six with a Top 25 ranking in the US LBM Coaches Poll , the Broncos would appear to have the inside track to the field of 12. But do they? Obviously, they must first secure the Pac-12 championship, and it helps that they’ll get to face primary challenger Oregon State on their home blue turf. But there’s a team from their former conference that might also have an argument. New Mexico is in the driver’s seat in the Mountain West, and also has just one competitive loss against a Power Four team. Things might get a bit testy between fans of those former league mates in early December should they win out. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Crisis in SEC, Big Ten lead college football overreactions after Week 8

item.title: ‘I’m Not Panicking,’ ‘This Loss Means Very Little’ — Chiefs’ Perfect Start Ends in Seattle, but NFL Analysts Aren’t Sweating It
item.description: Seattle Seahawks kicker Jason Myers (5) kicks a field goal against the Kansas City Chiefs during the third quarter at Lumen Field. For five weeks, the Kansas City Chiefs kept finding ways to win, even when games got tight. But against the Seattle Seahawks, they looked nothing like the team that had started the season unbeaten. Seattle shut down Patrick Mahomes, stifled the offense, and sent Kansas City home with a humbling 20-3 loss. Still, one bad night doesn’t erase everything the Chiefs have done this season. Several Pro Football Network analysts aren’t ready to hit the panic button, arguing that Seattle’s defense and home-field advantage deserve a lot of credit for Sunday’s result. PFN Analysts Explain Why Chiefs Shouldn’t Panic After Seahawks Loss Seattle held Mahomes to just 165 passing yards, no touchdowns and one interception. The Chiefs finished with only 213 total yards and failed to reach the red zone for the first time in Mahomes’ career. Harrison Butker missed field goals from 58 and 45 yards, while Kansas City’s only points came on a 50-yard kick. Seattle’s defense also kept former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III in check, limiting him to 36 yards on 14 carries after he entered the game averaging 133 rushing yards per contest. Despite the lopsided score, PFN analyst Jacob Infante urged fans not to overreact. “I’m not panicking over the Chiefs’ loss to the Seahawks on Sunday night,” he said, pointing to Seattle’s elite defense and home-field advantage. Infante added that Kansas City’s offense had played well for most of the season and said he would view the performance as an outlier unless further regression follows. PFN’s Brandon Austin also urged fans to give Seattle credit rather than read too much into Kansas City’s struggles. “Not reading too much into this one. The Seahawks dominated, but let’s give them some credit,” he said. Austin added that the Chiefs remain one of the league’s better teams when healthy and noted that no team has established itself as the clear favorite this season. Alex Kennedy pointed to Rashee Rice’s injury and Tyquan Thornton’s placement on injured reserve as factors exposing Kansas City’s limited receiver depth. He also noted that Jaylon Moore’s absence has hurt the offensive line and believes the Chiefs could be a team to watch as the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Kennedy said, “Looking ahead, I think Kansas City is a buyer to watch as the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches, and adding a wide receiver would be smart given their lack of depth.” Kennedy called a trade for Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. a potential game-changer, though he considers it unlikely. He also named three other possible targets. “Jerry Jeudy and Calvin Ridley’s names have surfaced in the rumor mill, but a sneaky target could be Chris Godwin Jr. if the Bucs drop their next two games (vs. Atlanta and at Chicago) before the deadline,” Kennedy said.

Kyle Soppe also viewed the loss as a bigger statement about Seattle than a reason to doubt Kansas City. He called the Seahawks a legitimate threat to repeat as champions and said they have the consistency needed to win games in January. Soppe said, “Great teams facing off, in my opinion, tell us more about the ceiling of the victor than build in worries about the loser, and this is a prime example.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Jason Katz was similarly unfazed, writing, “No team goes undefeated,” and predicting Kansas City would bounce back against the Denver Broncos next week. Katz said, “The Chiefs played a very good Seahawks team and were stymied by their elite defense. I fully expect them to bounce back next week and take down the Broncos.” After Week 7, the Seahawks rank No. 2 in the league with a PFN Defense Impact Score of 89.1, while the Chiefs are at No. 12 with a 78.5 grade. NFL reporter Josh Dubow also noted how unusual Kansas City’s offensive struggles were. The 20-3 loss marked only the second time in Patrick Mahomes’ career that the Chiefs scored three points or fewer. The other instance came in a 27-3 loss to Tennessee in October 2021, also in Week 7. For the analysts, Sunday’s defeat is a setback, not a reason to write off Kansas City’s season. The Chiefs will have a chance to bounce back next week when they visit the Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Crystal Palace fans comments before AND after losing to Newcastle United
item.description: Crystal Palace fans eating pizza Newcastle United Some interesting comments from Crystal Palace fans before AND after losing to Newcastle United. Two teams that were separated by only a point before kick-off. However, Crystal Palace fans seeing their club end the weekend one place off the relegation zone whilst Newcastle United are now eighth. Both Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle were under pressure to get a win on Sunday. Intriguing to look at what the Crystal Palace fans had to say before AND after the defeat to United. Crystal Palace fans commenting on their Holmesdale message board: PRE-MATCH ‘No way we keep a clean sheet. If we win it will be something like 3-2.’ ‘There’s no way we’re keeping a clean sheet, but the toon have got their own problems, so 3-2 to us’ ‘I predict that after the match it will be suggested that whichever manager has just lost should be sacked. That’s pretty well where we are as a society.’ ‘Watching Spurs and Cov and they both look better than us, can’t see how we can beat Newcastle unless we improve 200%.’ ‘Newcastle have lost 3 out of their last 4 games and these games included 2 Away defeats both 4-1. I would not be surprised if we attain some points from this game.’ ‘We’ll come second’ ‘A polite thought to all real palace out there. Pierre sage has not had our best striker, our best winger and joined us for a great support we have/ still have? f… Newcastle and lets get 3points sunday.’ ‘Newcastle are a bunch of self centered…. who think they are bigger than they are and need a damn good thrashing.’ ‘Lets all thump Newcastle so hard they begin speaking a comprehensible English.’ ‘Y I, give ’em some Eke Thump.’ ‘My heart says 3-1 Palace, my head says 3-1 Newcastle if Barnes and Elanga play.’ ‘I have in mind a 2-1 /3-1 victory against a Newcastle team who have lost key players.’ ‘Newcastle are not the best of travellers and haven’t seen anything this season that would suggest they have fixed that against anyone that puts them on the back foot. 2-0.’ POST-MATCH ‘Jaissle clearly got his players going for the second half and it paid off. Stupid to just hope the players will motivate themselves……’ ‘I see Sage has laid the blame on the players not coming out with the right mindset etc, after halftime.’ ‘Maybe Eddie Howe could be persuaded.’ ‘I waiting for somebody to say we’re only 6 points off a Champions League place.’ ‘After the optimism from Thursday’s performance, it was doubly disappointing to perform so poorly and lose so easily against a bang average Newcastle. To me it evidenced the theory that the European teams we play against are not as strong as a typical Premier League outfit. I came away from the game both angry and frustrated by what I had just seen.’ ‘The team started well, but we didn’t carve out any clear chances. There were a couple of times the ball pinged round the Newcastle box. Then our levels dropped a bit and the first half was drab. The wind didn’t help and Newcastle handled the conditions bet
