Crystal Palace fans commenting on their Holmesdale message board: PRE-MATCH ‘No way we keep a clean sheet. If we win it will be something like 3-2.’ ‘There’s no way we’re keeping a clean sheet, but the toon have got their own problems, so 3-2 to us’ ‘I predict that after the match it will be suggested that whichever manager has just lost should be sacked. That’s pretty well where we are as a society.’ ‘Watching Spurs and Cov and they both look better than us, can’t see how we can beat Newcastle unless we improve 200%.’ ‘Newcastle have lost 3 out of their last 4 games and these games included 2 Away defeats both 4-1. I would not be surprised if we attain some points from this game.’ ‘We’ll come second’ ‘A polite thought to all real palace out there. Pierre sage has not had our best striker, our best winger and joined us for a great support we have/ still have? f… Newcastle and lets get 3points sunday.’ ‘Newcastle are a bunch of self centered…. who think they are bigger than they are and need a damn good thrashing.’ ‘Lets all thump Newcastle so hard they begin speaking a comprehensible English.’ ‘Y I, give ’em some Eke Thump.’ ‘My heart says 3-1 Palace, my head says 3-1 Newcastle if Barnes and Elanga play.’ ‘I have in mind a 2-1 /3-1 victory against a Newcastle team who have lost key players.’ ‘Newcastle are not the best of travellers and haven’t seen anything this season that would suggest they have fixed that against anyone that puts them on the back foot. 2-0.’ POST-MATCH ‘Jaissle clearly got his players going for the second half and it paid off. Stupid to just hope the players will motivate themselves……’ ‘I see Sage has laid the blame on the players not coming out with the right mindset etc, after halftime.’ ‘Maybe Eddie Howe could be persuaded.’ ‘I waiting for somebody to say we’re only 6 points off a Champions League place.’ ‘After the optimism from Thursday’s performance, it was doubly disappointing to perform so poorly and lose so easily against a bang average Newcastle. To me it evidenced the theory that the European teams we play against are not as strong as a typical Premier League outfit. I came away from the game both angry and frustrated by what I had just seen.’ ‘The team started well, but we didn’t carve out any clear chances. There were a couple of times the ball pinged round the Newcastle box. Then our levels dropped a bit and the first half was drab. The wind didn’t help and Newcastle handled the conditions better. The start if the second half was a bit weird. All the half time people, kids entertainment, Pete and Alice, groundstaff were still on the pitch when the teams came out and the Palace players didn’t seem switched on. Unfortunately Newcastle were right on it, had 3 chances and scored 3 times. Even the offside decision failed to rouse Palace from their slumber.’ ‘Don’t you think the fact we can’t defend or attack well might be due to the manager. This squad isn’t great but it isn’t worse than Hull, Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham or Coventry for example. A competent manager would have more points than Sage and can still keep us up.’ ‘Man City might save us.’ ‘Not if we are bottom as that’s how it looks at the moment.’ ‘Players look lost and seem not bothered manager out of his depth.’ ‘For those that have consistently said selhurst doesn’t need the HF as the atmosphere is excellent without them, do any of you still back that claim, surely the jury is out. ‘Shall we sing a song for you’ the away fans sing. Our atmosphere is awful, such a shame and no it’s not about results, the HF backed the team win , lose or draw. It’s easy to sing when winning, every club does it. Bad atmosphere, bad defensive tactics, concerning times for our club, just when a 12th man is needed.’ ‘Maybe they will reform next season in the Championship.’ ‘ Basically without a couple of hundred vocal HF fans with a drum driving the chants our support is embarrassing,even worse than Fulham!! Even with them our home form was poor!!Now we are so weak on the pitch the lack of atmosphere makes things seem even worse. Very worrying times, relegation is a very serious threat.’ ‘A total of 12 goals conceded in our last 4 games, this is relegation form and these vulnerabilities HAVE to be addressed as a matter of priority. Yesterday, but for a marginal offside decision we would have lost 3-0 at Home which is unacceptable.’ ‘ Newcastle came to us on the back of 3 defeats in their last 4 games and lost 4-1 in their last 2 Away games.Yesterday they were distinctly mediocre but once again we found a way to lose.’ ‘1st goal, that cross was perfect, any player touching it a very good chance of it going in. 2nd one Wharton was awful, over slow getting up and not pick up the runner. Realistically that was the only real threat they did all match.’ ‘Parish earns £2.8M a year 3rd highest in Prem I think you’ll find Yet we’re 17th in the League.’ ‘Hull, Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham and Coventry did not sell their 3 best defensive players over the past 9 months.’ ‘Sage is absolutely clueless. The players look clueless. Made Newcastle look good. Sage needs to go.’ ‘A not particularly good Newcastle came out wanting a result, Palace just we’re not up to doing battle.’ ‘It’s famously hard to play well after a Thursday night in Europe. Several players have played very badly individually. Newcastle’s goals were actually quite good. If Sage had more credit in the bank, we’d probably not be talking about him today.’ Source

item.title: Will anyone end Spain's domination of women's Ballon d'Or?
item.description: Alessia Russo (left) and Khadija Shaw (right) are among the contenders seeking to deny Alexia Putellas (centre) a third Ballon d'Or [BBC] When the Ballon d'Or for best female footballer is dished out on Monday night, the chances are it will be a familiar figure that lifts the coveted trophy. Spanish icons Aitana Bonmati and Alexia Putellas have hoovered up the past five awards - and Putellas is favourite to win it for a third time. In May, the now London City Lionesses forward captained Barcelona to a quadruple, including a third Champions League trophy in four years and their seventh straight Liga F title. Arguably, the only reason Bonmati is not in the running this time is because of a serious leg injury suffered on international duty in November 2025. So will Putellas clean up once again? Is this trophy yet another example of Spain's increasing dominance of the women's game? Or does anyone else on the 30-strong shortlist stand a chance of wrenching it from her grasp? Why have Spain ruled this trophy? [BBC] The reasons are obvious. In Barcelona, Spain boast the world's most dominant club side. The Catalans have contested seven of the past eight Champions League finals (winning four) and have been domestic champions every year since 2019-20, clinching the title by an average of 15 points above second place in that time. Then, there is the national team. World champions in 2023, losing finalists at the Euros to England in 2025 and then winners of the Nations League last December, beating Germany in the final. At the heart of all this success has been Putellas, who scored 21 goals and produced 13 assists during Barcelona's sensational season. And it is not just her output that makes her case. Her all-round influence captaining an already stellar side cannot be overstated. So, with 38 trophies in her possession already, the 2021 and 2022 Ballon d'Or winner appears poised to take it once again. "Give it to her!" Spanish football expert Guillem Balague told BBC Sport. "Along with Marta, she is the best player in history. No doubt she was the best player in this campaign – and she won everything!" Unsurprisingly, Spain have more players on the shortlist than any other nation (six) and eight of the starting line-up from the Champions League final are in the running for this award. Among them are star striker Claudia Pina, who recently scored four against Real Madrid, goalkeeper Cata Coll and midfielder Patri Guijarro. Who could topple the favourite? Khadija Shaw scored 21 goals in the league last season to fire Manchester City to their first title in a decade, adding another five in the FA Cup as they completed the double. item.content:encoded: Alessia Russo (left) and Khadija Shaw (right) are among the contenders seeking to deny Alexia Putellas (centre) a third Ballon d'Or [BBC] When the Ballon d'Or for best female footballer is dished out on Monday night, the chances are it will be a familiar figure that lifts the coveted trophy. Spanish icons Aitana Bonmati and Alexia Putellas have hoovered up the past five awards - and Putellas is favourite to win it for a third time. In May, the now London City Lionesses forward captained Barcelona to a quadruple, including a third Champions League trophy in four years and their seventh straight Liga F title. Arguably, the only reason Bonmati is not in the running this time is because of a serious leg injury suffered on international duty in November 2025. So will Putellas clean up once again? Is this trophy yet another example of Spain's increasing dominance of the women's game? Or does anyone else on the 30-strong shortlist stand a chance of wrenching it from her grasp? Why have Spain ruled this trophy? [BBC] The reasons are obvious. In Barcelona, Spain boast the world's most dominant club side. The Catalans have contested seven of the past eight Champions League finals (winning four) and have been domestic champions every year since 2019-20, clinching the title by an average of 15 points above second place in that time. Then, there is the national team. World champions in 2023, losing finalists at the Euros to England in 2025 and then winners of the Nations League last December, beating Germany in the final. At the heart of all this success has been Putellas, who scored 21 goals and produced 13 assists during Barcelona's sensational season. And it is not just her output that makes her case. Her all-round influence captaining an already stellar side cannot be overstated. So, with 38 trophies in her possession already, the 2021 and 2022 Ballon d'Or winner appears poised to take it once again. "Give it to her!" Spanish football expert Guillem Balague told BBC Sport. "Along with Marta, she is the best player in history. No doubt she was the best player in this campaign – and she won everything!" Unsurprisingly, Spain have more players on the shortlist than any other nation (six) and eight of the starting line-up from the Champions League final are in the running for this award. Among them are star striker Claudia Pina, who recently scored four against Real Madrid, goalkeeper Cata Coll and midfielder Patri Guijarro. Who could topple the favourite? While Putellas is now tormenting Women's Super League defences in the blue of London City, it is another forward in this country that perhaps has the best case for consideration. Khadija Shaw scored 21 goals in the league last season to fire Manchester City to their first title in a decade, adding another five in the FA Cup as they completed the double. The Jamaica striker has been the WSL's top scorer for the past three seasons, scored 90 goals since her arrival in summer 2021 and was rewarded with a lucrative four-year deal in June. "We haven't had a major tournament but there are some amazing players on the list," said former England international Ellen White. "I would love to see Shaw up there - brilliant goalscoring." Shaw is part of a five-strong City contingent – they had none last season – but they all may fall short because they did not play in last season's Champions League. Arsenal's Alessia Russo was second to Shaw for goals last season and impressed in the Champions League, picking up nine goals. Last year, she came third in the Ballon d'Or voting last year behind Bonmati and club team-mate Mariona Caldentey. That came off the back of the Gunners' Champions League victory in May 2025. Exiting in the semi-finals to Lyon this year may cost her a shot at winning the award this year. One final candidate to break the Spanish stranglehold is, perhaps unsurprisingly, a Barcelona player. Poland's Ewa Pajor scored 11 goals in just 10 Champions League games last season, including a hat-trick in the final against Lyon. The 29-year-old won the Women's Gerd Muller trophy for top scorer last season and finished eighth in the overall rankings. Maybe it is her turn to take home the top prize. Russo and Greenwood nominated for Ballon d'Or What is the voting process - and why has it been controversial? The award covers the period from 3 August 2025 until 19 July 2025 and is based on individual performances, collective performances and fair play. Selected international journalists – one from each nation in the top 50 of the Fifa world rankings - rank their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. The Ballon d'Or is then awarded to the player with the highest total number of points. In previous seasons, the ceremony has come under fire for being too Euro-centric and for its scheduling during international breaks in the women's game. This year, the event is taking place during the domestic calendar, solving the date issue. However, the lack of US-based players from the National Women's Super League (NWSL) remains a fair criticism. One reason for this may be that the NWSL season runs from February to November and therefore does not marry with the dates this award covers. It means the likes of Washington Spirit's Trinity Rodman are notable absentees from a list purported to chart the world's best players. Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

item.title: Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde admits he played through pain against Barcelona: ‘Hopefully I’m not injured’
item.description: Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde admits he played through pain against Barcelona: ‘Hopefully I’m not injured’ Federico Valverde raised concerns over a possible hamstring injury after leaving Real Madrid’s 2-1 victory over Barcelona in El Clasico. The Real Madrid captain was substituted in the 62nd minute after appearing to struggle with pain in his leg, although the club had not announced a medical diagnosis by late Sunday night. Valverde started at right-back at Camp Nou and was seen clutching the back of his hamstring before Denzel Dumfries replaced him. The midfielder subsequently suggested the decision to withdraw him was precautionary, but his comments offered no definitive confirmation that he had avoided an injury. Valverde reveals pain after being substituted against Barcelona Speaking to Real Madrid TV , Valverde admitted he had been experiencing significant discomfort during the match. The captain also explained that he had agreed to continue playing when asked by the coach, underlining his determination to help his team secure an important result. “I had a lot of pain in my leg, but hopefully I’m not injured. “I think it was just a precaution. The coach asked me if I could play despite the pain, and of course I said yes. “The most important thing is to help the team win.” Jose Mourinho said after the match that Valverde had played more than 40 minutes while hurt. That raises questions over the extent of the problem, although the precise nature and severity of the suspected hamstring injury remain unconfirmed. Real Madrid await clarity over suspected hamstring problem Real Madrid had not published an official diagnosis as of late Sunday night, meaning any suggestion that Valverde has sustained a hamstring injury must be treated cautiously. The 62nd-minute substitution was an obvious concern given the pain he appeared to be experiencing, particularly with the midfielder playing an important role for the team. Medical examinations and an official update will be needed to establish whether he faces any spell on the sidelines. Valverde played through pain against Barcelona. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) For now, Valverde’s assessment offers some encouragement, but his hope that the problem is only precautionary should not be mistaken for confirmation that he has escaped injury. Valverde praises Mbappe and Lunin after El Clasico win Away from his own fitness concerns, Valverde congratulated Kylian Mbappe on reaching 100 goals for Real Madrid and praised Andriy Lunin for his contribution despite limited playing time. “Congratulations to both of them. Kylian has already overtaken me in terms of goals, even though he joined the club after I did… I’m absolutely delighted for him. “He’s working hard and he deserves it. He’s a great player, a star and a role model. I’m delighted he’s continuing to score goals for us because it’s important. “As for Lunin, there are no words to describe what he’s done today and what he does every day.

item.title: When is the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony?
item.description: When is the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony? The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony will take place this evening in a special 70th-anniversary awards. Football’s greatest individual accolade will be handed out, with Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal, and Kylian Mbappe among the frontrunners for the famous trophy. Here are all the details you need to know. Where and when is the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony? The 2026 Ballon d’Or awards ceremony will take place on Monday 26th October at the London Palladium Theatre. It’s the first time the awards have been presented in London, as a tribute to the accolade’s first winner, Stanley Matthews, on the 70th anniversary of the Ballon d’Or. The ceremony will commence at 8pm GMT and will be hosted by former Arsenal striker Thierry Henry and broadcaster Kate Scott. Which awards will be presented at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony? • The Men’s and Women’s Ballon d’Or® • The Men’s and Women’s Young Talent of the Year • The Men’s and Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year • The Men’s and Women’s Coach of the Year • The Men’s and Women’s Club of the Year • The Men’s and Women’s Striker of the Year • Sócrates Award, presented by L’Équipe and Peace and Sport for solidarity initiatives and societal causes supported by a committed champion. item.title: Barcelona are paying the price for a problem they should have anticipated in the summer
item.description: Barcelona are paying the price for a problem they should have anticipated in the summer Barcelona’s 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid has once again raised questions about the club’s defensive planning. While Hansi Flick’s side still possess plenty of quality, the lack of depth at centre-back is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. The concern is not simply that Barcelona have defensive weaknesses. Every team does, in one department or another. The bigger issue is that the club entered the season knowing its options had been reduced, yet failed to bring in a replacement. With Ronald Araujo and Alvaro Cortes leaving during the summer, Barcelona lost two centre-backs without signing anyone to fill the gaps they left behind. For a team competing for La Liga and the Champions League, that was always a considerable risk, and they are facing the full brunt of it now. Barcelona had opportunities to strengthen What makes it worse is that there was no shortage of potential options in the summer market to reinforce the central defence. Alessandro Bastoni was one of the more expensive possibilities at around €70 million, while Castello Lukeba was valued at approximately €60 million. Other names included Luka Vuskovic at €54 million, Nico Schlotterbeck at €50 million and Goncalo Inacio at €45 million. Cristian Romero was also mentioned as a potentially more affordable option, with a price range of €30 million to €40 million. While these were the players’ valuations and not the actual asking prices, Barça should have at least made an attempt to sign one of these names. They had an entire transfer window to assess their defensive needs and identify a solution, but instead weakened an already problematic position. The warning signs were already there Barcelona’s defensive approach under Flick places considerable responsibility on the centre-backs. Playing with a high defensive line requires speed, concentration, positional awareness and the ability to defend large spaces. It is a demanding system even when everyone is fit and performing well. When injuries, suspensions or poor form enter the picture, a shortage of specialist defenders can quickly become a serious problem. Pau Cubarsi has already taken on enormous responsibility at a young age, while Gerard Martin has provided an important option in the back line. However, relying on the same players repeatedly, especially across several competitions, leaves little room for rotation or unexpected setbacks. That is exactly the situation Barça find themselves in now. With Andreas Christensen, Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia all injured, Flick has no other options to call upon. Everyone except the club seemed to realise that they had a gaping hole in defence, and that is not a good place to be. Deco deserves scrutiny for the decision Barcelona have suffered a lot defensively. While Hansi Flick’s side still possess plenty of quality, the lack of depth at centre-back is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. The concern is not simply that Barcelona have defensive weaknesses. Every team does, in one department or another. The bigger issue is that the club entered the season knowing its options had been reduced, yet failed to bring in a replacement. With Ronald Araujo and Alvaro Cortes leaving during the summer, Barcelona lost two centre-backs without signing anyone to fill the gaps they left behind. For a team competing for La Liga and the Champions League, that was always a considerable risk, and they are facing the full brunt of it now. Barcelona had opportunities to strengthen What makes it worse is that there was no shortage of potential options in the summer market to reinforce the central defence. Alessandro Bastoni was one of the more expensive possibilities at around €70 million, while Castello Lukeba was valued at approximately €60 million. Other names included Luka Vuskovic at €54 million, Nico Schlotterbeck at €50 million and Goncalo Inacio at €45 million. Cristian Romero was also mentioned as a potentially more affordable option, with a price range of €30 million to €40 million. While these were the players’ valuations and not the actual asking prices, Barça should have at least made an attempt to sign one of these names. They had an entire transfer window to assess their defensive needs and identify a solution, but instead weakened an already problematic position. The warning signs were already there Barcelona’s defensive approach under Flick places considerable responsibility on the centre-backs. Playing with a high defensive line requires speed, concentration, positional awareness and the ability to defend large spaces. It is a demanding system even when everyone is fit and performing well. When injuries, suspensions or poor form enter the picture, a shortage of specialist defenders can quickly become a serious problem. Pau Cubarsi has already taken on enormous responsibility at a young age, while Gerard Martin has provided an important option in the back line. However, relying on the same players repeatedly, especially across several competitions, leaves little room for rotation or unexpected setbacks. That is exactly the situation Barça find themselves in now. With Andreas Christensen, Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia all injured, Flick has no other options to call upon. Everyone except the club seemed to realise that they had a gaping hole in defence, and that is not a good place to be. Deco deserves scrutiny for the decision Barcelona have suffered a lot defensively. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Deco has earned praise for several aspects of Barcelona’s squad-building work, and that recognition should not disappear because of one questionable decision. However, good sporting management also means anticipating problems before they become obvious, and Deco should have seen this coming from miles away. The sporting director and the club’s recruitment department had to weigh the cost of signing another defender against the risk of entering a long season without sufficient cover. The defeat against Madrid cannot be blamed entirely on that decision. Football matches are shaped by tactics, individual performances and numerous other factors. Still, the results against PSG and Real Madrid shone a spotlight on a vulnerability that has been threatening to surface for a while now. Barcelona cannot expect Flick to maintain the same defensive intensity throughout the season without giving him enough reliable options. There is also a difference between trusting young players and placing excessive responsibility on them in unfair circumstances. Barcelona’s academy remains one of the club’s greatest strengths, but youth development should be complemented by recruitment in the market. The frustration for Barcelona supporters is that this was not an unforeseeable crisis. The risk was visible in the summer, and the club had time to address it. If anything has come out of these two disappointing games, it is that Barça simply cannot go on like this, and the onus is now on Deco to address the situation in the January transfer window.

item.title: Former NFL MVP Kurt Warner Draws 1-Word Line In The Sand as Fan Pitches Bolder Apology for Steelers-Saints Broadcast Blunder
item.description: Former NFL MVP Kurt Warner Draws 1-Word Line In The Sand as Fan Pitches Bolder Apology for Steelers-Saints Broadcast Blunder Former NFL MVP Kurt Warner had an eventful Sunday morning calling the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints at Stade de France for NFL Network with Dave Pasch and Jason Kelce. During the broadcast, he mixed up Steelers running back Jaylen Warren with Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren. He also brought up Santonio Holmes’ winning catch from Super Bowl XLIII and said on the air, “I hate those Terrible Towels.” After the game, Warner apologized for one of those moments and explained another. That wasn’t enough; one fan suggested that instead of an apology, he should trade his colors for Pittsburgh black and gold. Kurt Warner Ends a Long Day of Explaining, Apologizing After Steelers-Saints Broadcast Kurt slipped up on Jaylen Warren’s name on a big day for the Steelers running back, who ran 18 times for 101 yards and caught three passes for 36 more. Through Week 7, his 5.5 yards per carry ranks second among qualified rushers and ranked sixth in PFN’s NFL RB Impact Score with an 82.4 grade through six weeks. Warner spent Sunday explaining that his comments about the Steelers were all in good fun, despite revisiting the painful Super Bowl 43 loss during the NFL Network broadcast. The former Arizona Cardinals quarterback even admitted that he may have sounded salty while discussing Holmes’ infamous winning catch. But then one fan suggested there was only one way for Warner to prove he had no hard feelings toward Pittsburgh. Responding to Warner’s tweet about not sounding salty, a fan joked , “Only way to prove it is to don a Steelers jersey 🤷‍♂️ it’s rules 😅😅” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator The former NFL MVP needed only a single word and left no room for any debate. “NEVER!!!!” he replied . His earlier tweets needed more than one word, though. Addressing the name slip, Warner said, “Yes, I called JAYLEN Warren ‘Tyler’ today after calling Colts game & referencing him in today’s game… My bad, so sorry… unfortunately it won’t be my last time bc sometimes u just react & misspeak!” He also made a point of praising the player he’d misnamed, writing that “JAYLEN was awesome today, so hopefully I gave him enough LOVE at other times.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator In another moment, he hit at Pittsburgh tradition. Broadcaster Myron Cope had introduced the Terrible Towel in 1975, asking fans to bring yellow towels to a playoff game against the Baltimore Colts. “I hate those Terrible Towels,” Warner remarked, according to Pittsburgh radio host Andrew Fillipponi . The reason the Super Bowl 43 loss possibly stings Warner is because he had come agonizingly close to securing his second title. He had already won one with the St. Louis Rams. James Harrison intercepted Warner near the goal line and returned it 100 yards for a touchdown to end the first half.

He also brought up Santonio Holmes’ winning catch from Super Bowl XLIII and said on the air, “I hate those Terrible Towels.” After the game, Warner apologized for one of those moments and explained another. That wasn’t enough; one fan suggested that instead of an apology, he should trade his colors for Pittsburgh black and gold. Kurt Warner Ends a Long Day of Explaining, Apologizing After Steelers-Saints Broadcast Kurt slipped up on Jaylen Warren’s name on a big day for the Steelers running back, who ran 18 times for 101 yards and caught three passes for 36 more. Through Week 7, his 5.5 yards per carry ranks second among qualified rushers and ranked sixth in PFN’s NFL RB Impact Score with an 82.4 grade through six weeks. Warner spent Sunday explaining that his comments about the Steelers were all in good fun, despite revisiting the painful Super Bowl 43 loss during the NFL Network broadcast. The former Arizona Cardinals quarterback even admitted that he may have sounded salty while discussing Holmes’ infamous winning catch. But then one fan suggested there was only one way for Warner to prove he had no hard feelings toward Pittsburgh. Responding to Warner’s tweet about not sounding salty, a fan joked , “Only way to prove it is to don a Steelers jersey 🤷‍♂️ it’s rules 😅😅” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator The former NFL MVP needed only a single word and left no room for any debate. “NEVER!!!!” he replied . His earlier tweets needed more than one word, though. Addressing the name slip, Warner said, “Yes, I called JAYLEN Warren ‘Tyler’ today after calling Colts game & referencing him in today’s game… My bad, so sorry… unfortunately it won’t be my last time bc sometimes u just react & misspeak!” He also made a point of praising the player he’d misnamed, writing that “JAYLEN was awesome today, so hopefully I gave him enough LOVE at other times.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator In another moment, he hit at Pittsburgh tradition. Broadcaster Myron Cope had introduced the Terrible Towel in 1975, asking fans to bring yellow towels to a playoff game against the Baltimore Colts. “I hate those Terrible Towels,” Warner remarked, according to Pittsburgh radio host Andrew Fillipponi . The reason the Super Bowl 43 loss possibly stings Warner is because he had come agonizingly close to securing his second title. He had already won one with the St. Louis Rams. James Harrison intercepted Warner near the goal line and returned it 100 yards for a touchdown to end the first half. Warner’s Cardinals still took a 23-20 lead on a 64-yard Larry Fitzgerald touchdown with a couple of minutes left. Then Ben Roethlisberger hit Holmes for a 6-yard score with 35 seconds remaining. The catch was upheld on review, and the 27-23 win gave Pittsburgh its sixth Super Bowl title. Warner finished 31-of-43 for 377 yards and three touchdowns. Holmes was named MVP with nine catches for 131 yards. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor When he was called out for sounding bitter, Warner pushed back after the game: “People, I’m just having a little fun at my Super Bowl loss to the Steelers, relax, please! I’m not bitter, I know SA had his feet down & they should have won… but like anyone, I don’t take myself too seriously & can still have fun with it all.” “It’s how normal life works – back and forth between rivals or after an important game… no need to CUSS me out for fun comments!” The Steelers moved to 5-2 with the win and sit second in the AFC North. They return to Acrisure Stadium to host the Cleveland Browns on Nov. 1. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: PSG XI v Lyon: Ferran Torres starts, Ousmane Dembélé to attend Ballon d’Or ceremony
item.description: PSG XI v Lyon: Ferran Torres starts, Ousmane Dembélé to attend Ballon d’Or ceremony PSG host Lyon tonight in Matchday 8 of the Ligue 1 campaign. The game was initially set to be played on Sunday night, but LFP agreed to move the game at the request of the Paris Police Prefecture as large-scale demonstrations were expected in Paris over the weekend. For the second year in a row, PSG will play a Ligue 1 game as the Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place. Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembélé is expected to attend the 2026 ceremony given he has sustained a thigh injury during last week’s UEFA Champions League 4-2 win over FC Barcelona. He’s not the only high-profile Parisien to miss out through injury. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffers from a potentially season-ending ACL tear. Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos are also out. Luis Enrique is set to turn to 2026 World Cup winner Ferran Torres to lead the line. With Kvaratskhelia out for the foreseeable, in-form France international Désiré Doué will occupy the left flank, and leave his right-wing spot to Maghnes Akliouche. PSG likely line-up v Lyon Matvey Safonov; Lucas Digne, Willian Pacho, Illia Zabarnyi, Achraf Hakimi; Warren Zaïre-Emery, Vitinha, João Neves; Désiré Doué, Ferran Torres, Maghnes Akliouche. (L’Éq) GFFN | Bastien Cheval

item.title: Thunder star Jalen Williams suffers horror injury as teammates fight back tears
item.description: Jalen Williams of the Oklahoma City Thunder was stretchered off the floor on Sunday evening after suffering a serious lower left leg injury while being fouled, a distressing moment that left several of his teammates visibly emotional. The injury occurred during a drive with 1::green-background[14] remaining in Oklahoma City ’s game against the Los Angeles Clippers . Medical personnel immediately tended to Williams after he fell beneath the basket on the Thunder's offensive end. With towels draped over Williams’ ankle, players from both teams reacted with immediate shock and dismay as the stretcher was brought onto the court. The contest was delayed about five minutes before the Thunder secured a 108-101 victory. Jalen Williams #8 of the Oklahoma City Thunder gives a thumbs up to the crowd while being carted off after an injury during the second half against the LA Clippers (Getty) "Just feel bad for him," Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said in a postgame televised interview, fighting back tears as he spoke. "Nothing more than that." The Thunder offered no immediate diagnosis, though the injury's severity was evident, prompting a stretcher call within seconds of the play ending. Oklahoma City coach Mark Daigneault said the team would receive a full briefing on Monday morning about Williams’ condition. "We’re not doing great," Daigneault said. Seated upright on the stretcher, Williams gave two thumbs-up signals to the cheering home crowd as they wheeled him away from the court. The Thunder offered no immediate diagnosis, though the injury's severity was evident, prompting a stretcher call within seconds of the play ending (Reuters) "Our whole city will have JDub in our thoughts and prayers as he deals with this adversity and as he makes his way through his recovery," Oklahoma City Mayor David Holt posted on social media after the game. Williams, a shooting guard who entered Sunday’s game averaging 18 points per game over his first 250 NBA contests, has already earned All-Star and All-NBA honors and played a key role in the Thunder's 2025 championship run. Last season, he missed 49 games due to various physical setbacks, primarily hamstring troubles and recovery following significant surgery on his right wrist. "He just loves playing, loves the competition," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "That’s who he is. ... It’s unfortunate, his luck so far. But he’s equipped for it." Oklahoma City returns to action on Monday night at home against the Phoenix Suns . The rapid turnaround gives the Thunder little choice but to move forward quickly, according to Daigneault. "We don’t have a choice," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "It’s what we signed up for. It’s obviously going to be tough without a player like that. He’s not gone forever. He’ll be back better than ever. We know it. We’ve just got to hold the fort down until he comes back."

item.title: “I think we were still in the bus when Hibs scored the goal,” Martin O’Neill
item.description: “I think we were still in the bus when Hibs scored the goal,” Martin O’Neill Martin O’Neill was naturally delighted to leave Easter Road yesterday afternoon with all three points as the Hoops maintained their four point advantage at the summit of the Scottish Premiership, but despite a below par display, the Celtic manager hailed it as our ‘best win of the season’… 25th October 2026; Easter Road, Scottish Premiership Football, Hibernian versus Celtic; Celtic manager Martin O’Neill and the Celtic bench react after Owen Elding of Hibernian shoots and scores to make it 1-0 in the 3rd minute. Photo Vagelis Georgariou That comment is sure to raise eyebrows among the hard to please Celtic supporter base, considering Hibs are rock bottom of the Premiership and went toe to toe with Celtic for the entire ninety plus minutes. Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, the veteran Irishman said: “I thought, given the circumstances, given the conditions, given the fact that we didn’t play all that well, I thought it was our best win of the season. I honestly did. “I’m really delighted. Delighted” 25th October 2026; Easter Road ; Scottish Premiership Football, Hibernian versus Celtic; Celtic manager Martin O’Neill and the Celtic bench react after Owen Elding of Hibernian shoots and scores to make it 1-0 in the 3rd minute. Photo Vagelis Georgariou “I thought it was our best win of the season. Difficult to come here in normal circumstances and to come from a goal behind after a couple of minutes as well too, I’m really delighted. Delighted.” Martin was a shocked as everyone to concede so early , and bemoaned the opportunities spurned by his players, particularly in the first half, with Kasper Hogh the main culprit, although he stopped short of mentioning names. 25th October 2026; Easter Road, Scottish Premiership Football, Hibernian versus Celtic; Owen Elding of Hibernian celebrates with his team mates after he shoots and scores to make it 1-0 in the 3rd minute. Photo Vagelis Georgariou “We were still in the bus when Hibs scored the goal” He said: “I think we were still in the bus when Hibs scored the goal, really travelling here. We had a number of chances maybe that we could have capitalised on in the first half, didn’t do so. “But we saw it through at the end. It was a difficult afternoon, but I was delighted with the side, delighted with the resilience and delighted with the way that they adapted eventually to the conditions.” Martin accepted that come the end of the campaign he may well look back on this match as one of the most significant if Celtic go on to win sixth consecutive title, which would be 15 Scottish Premiership triumphs in 16 seasons. 25th October 2026; Easter Road, Scottish Premiership Hibernian versus Celtic; Cameron Carter Vickers of Celtic leads the Celtic players in applauding the fans. 25th October 2026; Easter Road; Scottish Premiership Football, Hibernian versus Celtic; Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrates with Mika Baur of Celtic after he

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
item.description: At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby. Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher. Continue reading...

item.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
item.description: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.” Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. Continue reading...

item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
item.description: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone Braga and Miller give Hearts 2-0 win at Motherwell Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road. After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Continue reading...

item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Nicolas Jackson double sees Aston Villa end Manchester City’s perfect start
item.description: Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
